IntroducedBillHeader.Sponsors: Representatives O'Brien, Strow, Roberts, Talcott, Moeller and Ericks

Bill.BriefDescription: Providing a salary bonus for teachers who have professional certification.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to salary bonuses for certificated instructionalstaff attaining state professional certification; adding a new sectionto chapter 28A.405 RCW; and creating a new section.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature finds that the professionalcertification process required of new teachers and experienced teachersfrom outofstate is intended to advance their teaching skills anddemonstrate their ability to improve student learning. The legislaturealso finds that professional certification is a rigorous and demandingprocess, yet the state salary schedule does not recognize theseadvanced skill levels. Furthermore, teachers often pay substantialcosts to complete the programs, but are not reimbursed for theirexpenses. Therefore the legislature intends to address theseinequities by providing a bonus for all teachers who have achievedprofessional certification.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 28A.405RCW to read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Certificated instructional staff who have attained a p. 1 HB 2729professional certificate under rules adopted by the professionaleducator standards board or its predecessor agency shall receive anannual bonus beginning the school year immediately following theircertification. (2) The bonus for professional certification is provided inaddition to compensation received under a district's salary scheduleadopted in accordance with RCW 28A.405.200 and shall not be included incalculations of a district's average salary and associated salarylimitations under RCW 28A.400.200. (3) The bonus shall be paid in monthly increments and shall beincluded in the definition of "earnable compensation" under RCW41.32.010(10). The amount of the bonus shall be established by thelegislature through the omnibus appropriations act and is not part ofbasic education.
